pages.text: $(thing)Slow-scan television$() sends a picture, in colour, to everyone listening (or to one callsign) in about half a minute. The $(item)SSTV$() program does it through a radio interface cabled to the computer, on any band.$(br2)A picture coming in builds up line by line on the left. Lines that arrive while the radio cannot copy the signal come out as noise, so a weak or fading signal gives a torn picture, as on the air.

Pictures received are kept on the disk ($(thing)SSTV0001.IMG$()) and stay digital until printed. The gallery lists every picture on the disk:$(li)F3 sends the one picked (again).$(li)F4 writes a caption along the top and the bottom and saves it as a new picture.$(li)F5 prints it, F6 scans one in from the $(l:radiocraft:computer/scanner)scanner$(), Del deletes.$(li)L shows the picture coming in.
A blank floppy and a painting.
